DriedLeaves.name: Dried Leaves
DriedLeaves.description: Leaves become dry, brittle, brown or yellow and may eventually fall from the plant.
reason: Excessive heat or prolonged exposure to high temperature
Root damage or poor water absorption
Fungal infection or other plant disease
symptoms: Leaf edges become brown and dry
prevention: Maintain proper and regular irrigation
Avoid water stress and extreme heat
Maintain soil fertility
Check roots and control fungal infections when necessary
solution: Water the plant immediately with a deep, thorough irrigation and set a regular watering schedule
Provide shade or mulching around the base to reduce heat stress
Inspect roots for damage or rot and improve soil drainage if needed
Apply a balanced fertilizer with adequate potassium content
Remove severely dried leaves and treat with an appropriate fungicide if fungal infection is suspected

HealthyLeaves.name: Healthy Leaves
HealthyLeaves.description: Leaves are green, fresh, properly developed and show no visible signs of disease or pest damage.
HealthyLeaves.reason: The plant has suitable water, nutrients, light and growing conditions, with no significant pest or disease symptoms.
symptoms: No major spots, holes or drying
prevention: Continue proper irrigation
Provide balanced nutrients
Monitor the plant regularly for pests and diseases
Maintain good field hygiene
solution: No treatment needed; continue current care practices
Maintain regular irrigation and balanced fertilization schedule
Keep monitoring periodically to catch early signs of pests or disease
Maintain field hygiene and remove weeds around the plant

Mites.name: Mites
Mites.description: Mite infestation damages plant leaves by feeding on plant tissues and sucking plant sap.
symptoms: Small yellow or pale spots on leaves
prevention: Inspect the underside of leaves regularly
Maintain suitable irrigation and plant moisture
Remove heavily affected leaves when appropriate
Use recommended mite-control measures according to local agricultural guidance
solution: Spray plants with water to increase humidity and dislodge mites
Apply a recommended miticide or acaricide as per local agricultural guidelines
Introduce natural predators such as predatory mites or ladybugs if feasible
Prune and destroy heavily infested leaves to prevent spread
Avoid dust accumulation on leaves by regular cleaning

RedSpot.name: Red Spot
RedSpot.description: Red, reddish-brown or dark spots appear on the leaves and may enlarge if the underlying problem continues.
reason: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness
Infected plant material or contaminated field conditions
symptoms: Severe infection can cause leaf drying and falling
prevention: Improve air circulation around plants
Avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation
Remove severely infected plant material
Maintain field sanitation
Use appropriate disease-control measures when required
solution: Apply a suitable fungicide or bactericide as recommended by local agricultural experts
Prune affected leaves and branches to improve air circulation
Switch to drip irrigation instead of overhead watering to reduce leaf wetness
Remove and destroy infected plant debris away from the field
Correct any nutrient imbalance based on soil testing

YellowLeaf.name: Yellow Leaf
YellowLeaf.description: Leaves lose their normal green color and become yellow, either partially or across the entire leaf.
symptoms: Older leaves may yellow first in some nutrient deficiencies
Premature leaf fall in severe cases
prevention: Maintain balanced fertilizer application
Avoid both overwatering and underwatering
Ensure proper soil drainage
Inspect roots and leaves for pests or diseases
solution: Apply a nitrogen-rich or balanced fertilizer based on soil test results
Adjust watering schedule to avoid overwatering or underwatering
Improve soil drainage by loosening compacted soil or adding organic matter
Check and treat root damage or root disease if present
Control any pest infestation with appropriate measures

mawa.name: Mawa (Aphids)
mawa.description: Mawa, commonly referring to aphids, are small sap-sucking insects that feed on tender shoots, young leaves and plant stems.
reason: Presence and rapid multiplication of aphids
Presence of weeds or other host plants
symptoms: Small insects on young leaves and shoots
Sooty mold may develop on honeydew
prevention: Regularly inspect young leaves and shoots
Remove weeds and heavily infested plant parts
Encourage natural aphid predators where possible
Use recommended aphid-control measures according to local agricultural guidance
solution: Spray affected areas with a strong jet of water to dislodge aphids
Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil spray on infested shoots and leaves
Use a recommended insecticide as per local agricultural guidelines for severe infestations
Introduce natural predators like ladybugs or lacewings to control aphid population
Remove and destroy heavily infested shoots and nearby weeds
